info.description:
The ngrok REST API at https://api.ngrok.com provides programmatic access to provision and configure every ngrok resource: endpoints, domains, API keys, IP policies, tunnels, certificates, and more. Full documentation: https://ngrok.com/docs/api

**Authentication:** Send an API key as a bearer token: "Authorization: Bearer {API key}". Create and revoke keys at https://dashboard.ngrok.com/api-keys or via the /api_keys resource. Requests without credentials receive an error with code ERR_NGROK_200.

**Versioning and deprecation policy:** Every request must include the "ngrok-version: 2" header; a missing header returns HTTP 400 with error code ERR_NGROK_218. Version 2 is the current version; all earlier versions are deprecated. ngrok never makes breaking changes to a published API version. Breaking changes ship only as a new version that clients explicitly opt in to via this header. Additive changes (new resources, methods, and fields, and bug fixes that match documented behavior) may ship to a live version. Full policy: https://ngrok.com/docs/api#versioning-and-api-stability

**Rate limits:** By default, the API allows 120 requests per rolling 60-second window per account; some plans have higher limits. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with error code ERR_NGROK_226; wait for the window to pass before retrying. Details: https://ngrok.com/docs/errors/err_ngrok_226

**Errors:** Every 4xx and 5xx response carries the Error schema: the status_code, a human-readable msg, and in most cases a globally unique machine-readable error_code and a details object. Every error code is documented at https://ngrok.com/docs/errors
